findings.title: Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60s and the invalidation helper is never called
findings.body: The eligibility result is cached under a key derived only from organization id and project ids, with a 60 second TTL. Changes to `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` are therefore not visible for up to a minute. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (lines 67-74) exists for this purpose but nothing in the PR calls it, so it is dead code and the stale window cannot be cleared on allowlist changes. The docstring calls eventual consistency acceptable, but the allowlist is a rollout control, so a removed project can keep getting upsampled counts for a minute.

findings.title: Cache key built from Python hash() of the project id tuple
findings.body: The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(...)))` instead of the ids themselves. Distinct project sets can collide to the same key, which would return an eligibility answer computed for a different set of projects. Using the sorted id list (or a stable digest) in the key avoids this. The same expression is duplicated at line 73.

findings.title: Membership test is O(n*m) against a list allowlist
findings.body: `project_id in allowlist` runs against a list for each project, so the check is O(projects * allowlist size) and is repeated on every request. Converting the allowlist to a set once would be cheaper. This is minor unless the allowlist grows.

findings.title: Comments claim caching and late optimization that the code does not implement
findings.body: The comments say the eligibility check is a 'cached result' that 'ensures consistent behavior' and that the decision is stored 'to apply later ... allows for better query optimization and caching'. The code just calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and copies the boolean into `upsampling_enabled`. The transform is then applied in up to three places, each recomputing from `query_columns`. The comments mislead maintainers about what is cached and why, and the duplicated transform blocks should be collapsed into one.

findings.title: Unrelated change to a public error message
findings.body: The topEvents validation message changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is not part of the upsampling feature. Clients or tests matching the old string will break, and the change should be split out or justified.

findings.title: upsampled_count is only defined on the discover function converter
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count`, and that rewrite is applied whenever the dataset is `errors` (`_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True for it). The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is added only to the discover dataset's function converter. Unless the errors dataset shares this converter, queries on the errors dataset will fail with an unknown function error. The PR's tests only cover the discover path through the endpoint, so this is not caught.

findings.title: upsampled_count ignores the alias set by the caller and hard-codes sum(sample_weight)
findings.body: The function returns `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no guard for events lacking `sample_weight`. The comment says the schema guarantees this, but the transform is driven purely by project allowlist membership. An allowlisted project with events that have no sample_weight will silently produce 0 counts for those events, and nothing in the query path validates this assumption.

findings.title: Helper swallows all exceptions and is applied to every stored test event
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps its lookups and conversions in bare `except Exception: pass`. Failures are silently ignored, which makes test data problems hard to diagnose. It also runs for every event in `store_event`, so any test that stores an event with an `error_sampling` context now gets a `sample_rate` set implicitly. That side effect is not documented and is not limited to the upsampling tests.

findings.title: Stray submodule pointer committed to the repository
findings.body: The PR adds a file `sentry-repo` containing a submodule commit hash. It is unrelated to error upsampling and looks like an accidental commit. The PR description 'Test 3' also gives reviewers no context. Both should be removed or explained before merge.
